node_definition.done_when: No real scheduler verb runs in this node. Every case uses a recording scheduler on PATH in a temporary RECKON_HOME, and no allocation is submitted, adopted, cancelled or reloaded for real. The locked decision in f-tfsoa-handoff-01 is that the one shared allocation is the supervisor-running kind: an ambix-fleet or reckon-fleet batch job whose batch step runs fleet-supervisor, found by reckon/crew/fleet_node.py find_allocation and its job comment. The node builds on fleet_node.py and does not add a second hold path beside it. After the change, ensure_reservation, given no unkeyed record while fleet_node finds a live supervisor-running allocation, publishes that job to the unkeyed record at crew_home()/placement/reservation.json with the allocation's own declared shape (partition, cores, memory) read from the scheduler. It then submits nothing, and reports the job as adopted. With a record naming that job and a live probe, it reports already-held and submits nothing. With neither, it keeps its present hold behaviour. A resumed run is placed too: the crew resume launch path (reckon/crew/resumption.py and dispatch.resume_plan at reckon/crew/dispatch.py:8118) resolves placement through resolve_backend_placement exactly as dispatch does, so a resumed worker of a placement-declaring backend runs as a step with --overlap in the published job. tests/test_the_fleet_allocation_is_adopted.py asserts four things against the recording scheduler. First, one adoption from a recorded supervisor-running job with zero allocation-obtaining requests and the record naming that job id. Second, a second ensure under another project reading the same job with zero requests. Third, a resumed run placed as a step in the adopted job. Fourth, a backend declaring no placement untouched on resume. The declared negative control is executed and logged: remove the adoption branch in a scratch tree, and the first case logs one allocation-obtaining request and fails. The test files importing reckon.crew.placement, reckon.crew.fleet_node or reckon.crew.resumption are run at base and at head with pytest-xdist -n 8, each arm with its own --basetemp under /tmp, and they add no failing id. The comment at reckon/crew/placement.py around :344 that still says the project is carried in the path is corrected. Every log sits under the run directory, headed with revision, tree and literal command, and ends EXIT=, and basetemps are deleted afterwards. Only reckon/crew/placement.py, reckon/crew/fleet_node.py, reckon/crew/resumption.py, reckon/crew/dispatch.py (the resume-plan and placement-resolution regions only) and the new test file change.
